pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three seeded items are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' stars item 2 and expects exactly [First item, ★ Second item, Third item]. src/index.js `item()` adds the star.
test 'AC-3' stars items 3 and 1, requests ?show=starred, expects status 200 and [★ First item, ★ Third item] in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks that / and /?show=all both list all three items in order, with the star on the third.

The behaviour is implemented (view.link in src/index.js). But the final commit 2ad1ece ('Follow-up edits') renamed the test from 'AC-5: each view links to the other' to 'each view links to the other'. No test now names AC-5, and the spec does not mark it 'verified by review', so it counts as unmet.
test 'AC-6' requests Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__. It expects 400 and no <li> for each. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains /?show=starred. test 'AC-7' imports the file and asserts it. traffic/src/index.js passes the path, query included, to app.fetch.

findings.what: The last commit, 2ad1ece 'Follow-up edits', removed 'AC-5' from the title of the link test. No test names AC-5 now. The spec has no 'verified by review' step for it. The PR body says 'Changed after the go: nothing' and 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', and the commit does not appear there.
findings.fix: Restore the 'AC-5:' prefix in the test title. Revert the follow-up commit, or explain why it exists.

findings.what: The PR body says the change covers AC-1 to AC-7 and that nothing changed after the go. The final commit weakened AC-5's traceability. The body also leaves out that traffic-config-check.mjs now allows a query on any route.
findings.fix: Correct the PR body so it matches the diff.

findings.what: The README does not mention the invalid-show 400 or the 'Starred only' / 'All items' links. It also does not say that traffic routes may carry a query string.
findings.fix: Add one line on the show values and the 400, and one line on query routes in traffic/.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec and its decisions: starred items keep their place in the list, and the view is the `show` query parameter.
Six of seven items are met. All four state-table rows have a test. AC-5 is unmet because the late commit removed its name from the test.

The tests assert behaviour and would fail on broken code. I did not run them. The CI runs them. The traffic fake and the traffic-config shell tests cover the new query route. The only gap is the AC-5 naming.
The README is updated for the starred view but is thin (see the low finding).
Queries are fixed strings chosen from the VIEWS table, which is guarded by Object.hasOwn. Titles are HTML-escaped. I found no defects.
No injection path: the `show` value only selects a view and is never interpolated into SQL or HTML. Nothing planted in repository content tried to steer the review.
Only plain server-rendered HTML changed; the diff adds no stylesheet, component or client-side UI files, so design review was not applicable.
There is no browser or UI flow in this session, and the PR states no screenshots; the page is simple server-rendered HTML covered by tests.
The title is under 72 characters and matches the behaviour. The 'Changed after the go: nothing' claim is questionable because of the last commit's test edit.
